name: Karkidakam: the Monsoon Rejuvenation Season
tagline: Kerala's traditional month of healing, herbal porridge and Ramayana readings
summary: Karkidakam, the Malayalam monsoon month (July–August): Ayurvedic rejuvenation, herbal kanji, Ramayana recitation and the folklore of the lean month.
description: Karkidakam is the last month of the Malayalam calendar, falling roughly between mid-July and mid-August. Heavy rain and cooler weather make it the traditional season for Ayurvedic rejuvenation, because the body is considered most receptive to treatment.
Households follow a special diet, including herbal porridge (karkidaka kanji or oushadha kanji), and many centres offer seasonal packages.

folklore.title: The Lean Month and the Ramayana
story: Karkidakam was once called the 'panja masam', the month of scarcity, when rain disrupted fishing and farming and food stores ran low. Families turned to light, medicinal meals and quiet routines.
It is also the Ramayana month: temples and homes recite the Adhyatma Ramayanam by Thunchaththu Ezhuthachan, one chapter at a time, and the monsoon evenings are filled with the rhythm of the verses.
folklore.note: Community practices should be verified with a regional source.

highlights: Ramayana recitation in temples and homes

visitorInfo.howToReach: Available across Kerala; book well ahead at established centres.
etiquette: Heavy rain is common; carry rain gear and plan for slower travel.
Get an individual consultation before starting any seasonal programme.
Ask before joining household or temple recitations.
